doc: An adjustment above the limit needs a supervisor's PIN.
A storage location: a pick face (zone P) or a reserve rack (zone R).
The shipping label on an outbound carton, with ship-to, PO and carton number.
The 18-digit serial shipping container code (SSCC) with its check digit.
A count whose variance exceeds this goes back on the recount list.
Counted minus system quantity, relative to the system quantity.
A customer's order lines, each due on a truck cutoff.
Counting bins on a rolling schedule and reconciling the counted quantity with stock on hand.
Dangerous-goods classes that react with each other never share a pick cart.
Knowing what stock is in which bin and keeping that record right.
A stocked product, identified by its item number (SKU).
The printed list of a cart's lines in walking order.
Walking a cart's lines and confirming each pick by scanning the bin and then the item.
Topping up pick faces from reserve racks when they fall below their minimum.
An RMA: the permission for a customer to send goods back.
Receiving goods a customer sends back against an RMA and grading each line: restock, vendor return or scrap.
A manual correction of stock on hand, logged with who made it.
The quantity of one item in one bin, as the system records it.
Grouping the order lines due on one truck cutoff into pick carts.
Packs one cutoff's order lines into carts of at most cart_lines lines, splitting on incompatible hazmat classes.
Takes an uploaded count sheet, records each bin's variance and returns the bins to recount.
Renders a carton label as ZPL with an SSCC barcode.
The handheld page that prints a cart's lines and hosts the scan loop.
Finds pick faces below minimum and queues a move from the fullest reserve bin.
Grades each returned line A (restock), B (seconds), V (vendor return) or X (scrap) and closes the RMA.
The handheld loop: scan the bin, scan the item, confirm the line, go to the next bin.
